rationale: Olden/power is a small, arithmetic- and pointer-intensive tree-walking simulator, so cheap always-safe transformations are favored: SUB gets high benefit weights and near-zero costs since instruction substitution is essentially free on this compute-bound code. FLA receives the highest SecurityGain because flattening the tree-traversal control flow strongly resolves static analysis, with moderate runtime cost accepted since hot loops are simple; BCF is kept high on security but tempered by its high runtime/size costs given power's tight numeric kernels; IBR and ICALL add strong indirection-based resistance but carry the highest runtime penalties on this pointer-chasing workload, so their cost weights keep them selective rather than pervasive; SPLIT is a low-value enabler applied cheaply to improve FLA/BCF coverage; IGV is modest overall since the program has few globals and its static profile shows no source-level detail, arguing for conservative, low-risk indirection. All seven passes remain enabled but cost-weighted so the selection engine concentrates obfuscation on security-benefit dimensions while bounding overhead and correctness risk on this small benchmark with unknown function inventory.
